scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.
scenes.cap: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Caps are percentages, so position sizes rise, and so does market impact.
Add independent protocols and issuers before adding size to existing ones.
More size means more value at stake in custody
scenes.vo: Compounding: reinvesting the retained share grows principal, and income with it. At a 4.66% risk-adjusted yield with 30% retained, principal grows about 1.4% a year from retention alone. The payout grows at about the same rate: $16,310 to about $17,480 after five years (before any new capital). Scaling rules as the book grows: Check pool depth and exit liquidity at the new size. Annual review (one page): First, Caps are percentages, so position sizes rise, and so does market impact. Next, Add independent protocols and issuers before adding size to existing ones. Then, more size means more value at stake in custody: revisit Module 12.2. Also, Balance sheet: start versus end equity, L.T.V., runway. On top of that, Income: expected versus realised, by source.
scenes.cap: Compounding: reinvesting the retained share grows principal, and income with it. At a 4.66% risk-adjusted yield with 30% retained, principal grows ~1.4%/yr from retention alone. The payout grows at about the same rate: $16,310 → ~$17,480 after five years (before any new capital). Scaling rules as the book grows: Check pool depth and exit liquidity at the new size. Annual review (one page): First, Caps are percentages, so position sizes rise, and so does market impact. Next, Add independent protocols and issuers before adding size to existing ones. Then, more size means more value at stake in custody: revisit Module 12.2. Also, Balance sheet: start vs end equity, LTV, runway. On top of that, Income: expected vs realised, by source.

scenes.title: Key ideas (cont.)
scenes.vo: And Losses and near-misses: what happened, what changed. Plus, Payout: paid versus policy. One more: Risk assumptions: update loss probabilities from the year's incidents. And finally, Custody and succession drill: done?

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Exit liquidity checked at current size
Annual review completed and filed with the books
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Retained income reinvested per policy. Next, Exit liquidity checked at current size. And finally, Annual review completed and filed with the books.

scenes.q: Yield 5%, 40% retained. Growth from retention alone?
scenes.vo: Question one. Yield 5%, 40% retained. Growth from retention alone? [[pause 4]] The answer: about 2% a year.

scenes.q: Why check exit liquidity as the book grows?
scenes.a: A position that was easy to exit at $50k may move the market at $500k.
